detection_source_b.decision: source (b) kept for detections; every table using it must carry the flag DETECTOR_TRAIN_DATA_UNVERIFIED and may not be called held-out until the upstream exp file / training split is checked
evidence: HF dataset noahcao/dancetrack file list: only dancetrack_url.xlsx, train1/train2/val/test1/test2 zips (no detections file)
DanceTrack README: no detection files; trained models published at HF noahcao/dancetrack_models (license tag cc-by-4.0)
needs_to_use: ByteTrack/YOLOX code + exp file on Colab (torch, brittle with new numpy)
confirm which splits the checkpoint was trained on before claiming val is unseen
detection_source_b.open_item: verify training split from DanceTrack/ByteTrack exp files (train-only vs train+val) before any held-out claim

smoke.agreement: IoU 0.5 against val GT; precision is understated if the detector fires on non-dancers that GT does not label

checkpoint.architecture: YOLOX-X depth 1.33 width 1.25, 1 class, loads strict=True

smoke.fps_note: ~18 s per frame on Colab CPU for the first run: tier B detections need a GPU
smoke.frames: 9 val frames, 3 sequences (0004, 0026, 0063), frames at 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 of length; letterbox 800x1440, NMS 0.7

imagenet_rgb.verdict: correct: RGB /255 then ImageNet mean/std; the runner must use this

raw_bgr.verdict: wrong input scaling for this checkpoint

smoke_acceptance: checkpoint loads (state dict keys match YOLOX exp) and sha256 recorded
inference on >=1 frame returns person boxes
train-split provenance of the checkpoint documented (DanceTrack train only vs CrowdHuman/MOT mix); val counts as unseen only if val was not in training
if any check fails: drop source (b), record reason
detection_source_b.verdict: usable as a detector (loads, recall 0.986, precision 0.864 on 9 val frames). NOT established: that val is unseen by it. The checkpoint carries no training metadata and recall ~1.0 on val is what a model that saw val would also give.

protocol.environment_conflict: trackers==2.6.1 requires numpy>=2.0.2 but requirements.lock.txt pins numpy==1.26.4 -> tracking tier B is installed from requirements-tracking.txt in its own environment (Colab); the TrackEval shim in tracking_scoring.load_trackeval covers numpy 2.x and its 7 tests pass under numpy 2.4.6
protocol.frame_rate: per sequence from seqinfo.ini (library default 30.0 would mis-scale lost_track_buffer)

interface.botsort_reid: none: the library signature has no appearance model, BoT-SORT here = IoU association + camera motion compensation
interface.frame_argument: SORT/ByteTrack/OC-SORT ignore `frame` (pass None, they warn otherwise); BoT-SORT needs the frame for CMC and silently skips CMC when it is None, so the runner must pass frames for BoT-SORT or set enable_cmc=False explicitly
interface.rows_with_tracker_id_minus_1: unconfirmed tracks are returned with tracker_id == -1: drop them before writing MOT output

protocol.sampling: random search, seeded; the same seed and the same N for every family; config 0 = published default
protocol.selection: highest mean dev HOTA; ties -> lower config index
protocol.tuning_split: dev (8 train sequences, see stratification file)
